newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Kandir sees rates falling next year.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Kandir sees rates falling next year.

text.p: Brazilian Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said interest rates are likely to fall four percentage points and foreign direct investment to reach at least $10 billion next year, significantly reducing the country's public debt.

Kandir, in a business conference, said that the fall in interest rates, now at 23 percent to 24 percent a year, will cut Brazil's public debt by 8.0 billion reais and save about 1.5 billion reais in interest payments on that debt.
He also said that foreign direct investment has risen sharply since Brazil's Real anti-inflation Plan was introduced from $1.0 billion in 1993 to an estimated $7.5 billion this year.
Kandir said Brazil's two main economic woes are its large public debt and swelling external account deficits. But he noted the country is in a better position to handle them.
The Planning Minister also said that, due to the success of the Real Plan, Brazil no longer needs to build up its reserves and will be spending less on financial system aid.
"Reserves will not go up. They will probably come down a little," he said.
The country can also expect to benefit from an injection of $8.0 billion to $10 billion in privatization revenues next year.
"The privatization process is now entering a decisive phase," he said, referring to receipts coming mostly from telecommunications and power sectors.
